obligations.title: Add the duty: Assess and record the firm's money laundering and terrorist financing risks
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), reg. 18, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Assess and record the firm's money laundering and terrorist financing risks

summaries.en: A firm within the regulations must identify and assess, by appropriate steps, the money laundering and terrorist financing risks its business faces, looking at its customers, the countries it operates in, its products and services, its transactions and its delivery channels, and at information from its supervisor. It keeps an up-to-date written record of the steps taken, unless its supervisor has said in writing that none is needed, and gives the assessment and that record to the supervisor on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep written anti-money laundering policies, controls and procedures approved by senior management
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), reg. 19, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep written anti-money laundering policies, controls and procedures approved by senior management

summaries.en: The firm must establish, maintain and regularly review policies, controls and procedures that manage the risks found in its risk assessment, proportionate to its size and nature and approved by senior management, and keep a written record of them, of changes to them and of how they were communicated inside the business. They cover risk management, internal controls, customer due diligence, reliance and record keeping, compliance monitoring, the scrutiny of unusually complex or large transactions and the assessment of new products and technology before they are adopted. Where relevant they are communicated to branches and subsidiaries outside the United Kingdom.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Appoint a responsible senior officer and a nominated officer, screen staff and keep an independent audit function
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), reg. 21, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Appoint a responsible senior officer and a nominated officer, screen staff and keep an independent audit function

summaries.en: Where its size and nature make it appropriate, the firm must make a board member or senior manager responsible for compliance with the regulations, screen relevant employees before and during their appointment, and set up an independent audit function that tests its policies, controls and procedures. It must appoint a nominated officer and tell its supervisory authority who holds each post within 14 days of an appointment. It also keeps systems that let it answer fully and rapidly when financial investigators, constables or the other officers the regulation lists ask whether it has, or had in the previous five years, a business relationship with a person.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Train relevant staff and agents to recognise money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), reg. 24, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Train relevant staff and agents to recognise money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing

summaries.en: The firm must take appropriate measures so that relevant employees, and agents whose work is of the same kind, know the law on money laundering, terrorist financing, proliferation financing and data protection that bears on the regulations, and are regularly trained to recognise and deal with transactions and situations that may be related to them. It keeps a written record of the measures taken and the training given.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify and verify customers and beneficial owners and monitor the relationship
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), regs. 27 and 28, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Identify and verify customers and beneficial owners and monitor the relationship

summaries.en: The firm must apply customer due diligence when it establishes a business relationship, carries out an occasional transfer of funds above £800 or another occasional transaction of £12,000 or more, suspects money laundering or terrorist financing, or doubts identification information it holds, and to existing customers at appropriate times on a risk basis. It identifies the customer and verifies that identity, identifies any beneficial owner and takes reasonable measures to verify who that is, and assesses the purpose and intended nature of the relationship. It then monitors the relationship, scrutinising transactions and keeping its due diligence information up to date.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Stop transactions and end the relationship when due diligence cannot be completed
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), reg. 31, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Stop transactions and end the relationship when due diligence cannot be completed

summaries.en: Where the firm cannot apply the required customer due diligence measures to a customer, it must not carry out a transaction with or for that customer, must not establish a business relationship, and must end any existing one. It must also consider whether to make a disclosure under Part 7 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 or Part 3 of the Terrorism Act 2000. Money deposited may be repaid to the depositor, with the required consent where a disclosure has to be made.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply enhanced due diligence to high-risk cases and politically exposed persons
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), regs. 33 and 35, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Apply enhanced due diligence to high-risk cases and politically exposed persons

summaries.en: The firm must apply enhanced customer due diligence and enhanced ongoing monitoring in every case of high risk, among them business with a person established in a country on the Financial Action Task Force's call for action list, correspondent relationships, customers who are politically exposed persons or their family members or known close associates, and unusually complex or large transactions. It needs risk-management systems to find out whether a customer or beneficial owner is a politically exposed person. For such a customer it obtains senior management approval for the relationship, takes adequate measures to find out where the customer's wealth and the funds involved come from, and monitors the relationship more closely.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep due diligence and transaction records for five years
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/692), reg. 40, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep due diligence and transaction records for five years

summaries.en: The firm must keep copies of the documents and information obtained for customer due diligence, and enough supporting records of the transactions covered to reconstruct them. It keeps them for five years from the day it knows or has reasonable grounds to believe the occasional transaction is complete or the business relationship has ended; transaction records within a relationship need not be kept for more than 10 years. After that it deletes the personal data unless another enactment, court proceedings or the data subject's consent allows it to keep them.

titles.en: The Payment Services Regulations 2017

payload.officialRef: The Payment Services Regulations 2017, S.I. 2017/752

obligations.title: Add the duty: Safeguard funds received for payment transactions
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 23, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Safeguard funds received for payment transactions

summaries.en: An authorised payment institution must safeguard the sums it receives for the execution of payment transactions, either by keeping them apart from all other funds and, if still held at the end of the next business day, placing them in a designated safeguarding account at the Bank of England or at an authorised credit institution, or in secure, liquid assets the FCA approves, or by covering them with an insurance policy or comparable guarantee. It must keep organisational arrangements that minimise the risk of losing those funds through fraud, misuse, negligence or poor administration.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the payment service user the required information before the contract binds
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), regs. 43 and 48, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give the payment service user the required information before the contract binds

summaries.en: Before a user is bound by a single payment service contract, the provider must give or make available the identifier needed for the payment, the maximum execution time, the charges, any exchange rate and the parts of Schedule 4 that are relevant to the contract. Before a framework contract binds the user, it must provide in good time the full set of information listed in Schedule 4. Where the contract is concluded at the user's request by a means of distance communication that does not allow this, the information follows immediately afterwards.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Refund an unauthorised payment by the end of the next business day
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 76, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Refund an unauthorised payment by the end of the next business day

summaries.en: Where a payment was executed without the payer's consent, the provider must refund its amount and put the debited account back in the state it would have been in, as soon as practicable and at the latest by the close of the business day after it learns of the transaction. The time limit does not apply where the provider has reasonable grounds to suspect fraud by the user and reports those grounds in writing. Where the payment went through a payment initiation service provider, the account provider still makes the refund.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Credit the payee's provider by the end of the business day after the payment order is received
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 86, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Credit the payee's provider by the end of the business day after the payment order is received

summaries.en: The payer's provider must make sure the amount reaches the account of the payee's provider by the end of the business day following receipt of the payment order, or the second business day for a paper order. Where it has reasonable grounds to suspect the order follows fraud or dishonesty by someone other than the payer, it may delay the payment to make enquiries, for no longer than necessary and never beyond the fourth business day, and must tell the payer of the delay and the reasons.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report a major operational or security incident to the FCA without undue delay
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 99, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Report a major operational or security incident to the FCA without undue delay

summaries.en: A provider that learns of a major operational or security incident must notify the FCA without undue delay, in the form and with the content the FCA directs. If the incident affects or may affect the financial interests of its users, it must also tell them without undue delay about the incident and what they can do to limit its effects.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply strong customer authentication to online account access and electronic payments
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 100, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Apply strong customer authentication to online account access and electronic payments

summaries.en: A provider must apply strong customer authentication when a user accesses a payment account online, initiates an electronic payment or does anything through a remote channel that may carry a risk of payment fraud, and for remote electronic payments the authentication must link the transaction to a specific amount and payee. It must protect the confidentiality and integrity of users' security credentials, and an account provider must let payment initiation and account information providers rely on its authentication. Technical standards may set exemptions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Answer payment service complaints within 15 business days
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 101, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Answer payment service complaints within 15 business days

summaries.en: For users who cannot take a complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service, the provider must have and apply adequate and effective procedures for resolving complaints about rights and obligations under Parts 6 and 7. It must reply to every point on paper or another agreed durable medium within 15 business days of receiving the complaint. In exceptional cases beyond its control it sends a holding reply with reasons and a deadline no later than 35 business days after receipt.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give payment service providers access to payment account services on fair terms
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Services Regulations 2017 (S.I. 2017/752), reg. 105, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give payment service providers access to payment account services on fair terms

summaries.en: A credit institution must grant payment service providers, and applicants for authorisation or registration, access to payment account services on terms that are objective, proportionate and non-discriminatory, wide enough for them to provide payment services efficiently. It states its criteria when asked about access and keeps arrangements to apply them properly. If it refuses or withdraws access it must notify the FCA with reasons.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Safeguard funds received in exchange for electronic money
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/99), regs. 20 to 22, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Safeguard funds received in exchange for electronic money

summaries.en: An electronic money institution must safeguard the funds it has received in exchange for issued electronic money. It either keeps them apart from all other funds and, if still held at the end of the next business day, places them in a designated safeguarding account at the Bank of England or at an authorised credit institution, or in secure, liquid, low-risk assets held with an authorised custodian, or covers them with an insurance policy or comparable guarantee payable into such an account. Funds received by payment instrument are safeguarded once credited or made available, and at the latest five business days after the electronic money was issued.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold own funds of at least 350,000 euro or the calculated requirement at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/99), reg. 19, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Hold own funds of at least 350,000 euro or the calculated requirement at all times

summaries.en: An authorised electronic money institution must at all times hold own funds at least equal to the greater of 350,000 euro and the own funds requirement calculated under Schedule 2, as adjusted by any direction of the FCA. A small electronic money institution whose average outstanding electronic money reaches 500,000 euro must hold the amount calculated under paragraph 14 of that Schedule.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify the FCA before outsourcing an operational function and keep control of important ones
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/99), reg. 26, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Notify the FCA before outsourcing an operational function and keep control of important ones

summaries.en: An authorised electronic money institution must notify the FCA when it intends to contract out any operational function relating to issuing, distributing or redeeming electronic money or to providing payment services. An important operational function, an information technology system among them, may be outsourced only if the institution's internal control and the FCA's ability to monitor it are not impaired, senior management keeps its responsibility, and the institution's obligations to holders and the conditions of its authorisation are unaffected.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep records of compliance with the prudential rules for at least five years
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/99), reg. 27, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep records of compliance with the prudential rules for at least five years

summaries.en: An electronic money institution must maintain the records that relate to its compliance with Part 3 of the regulations, in particular those the FCA needs to supervise that compliance, and keep each for at least five years from the day it was created.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Issue electronic money at par and redeem it at par whenever the holder asks
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/99), regs. 39 to 41, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Issue electronic money at par and redeem it at par whenever the holder asks

summaries.en: An electronic money issuer must issue electronic money at par value without delay when it receives funds, and redeem the monetary value held at par at any time the holder asks. The contract must state the conditions of redemption and any fees clearly and prominently, and the holder is told of them before being bound. A redemption fee may be charged only if the contract states it and only for redemption before the contract ends, on early termination by the holder, or more than a year after termination, and it must be proportionate to the costs actually incurred.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay no interest or time-related benefit on electronic money
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/99), reg. 45, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Pay no interest or time-related benefit on electronic money

summaries.en: An electronic money issuer must not award interest for holding electronic money, or any other benefit linked to the length of time a holder holds it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give consumers a fee information document before a payment account contract
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), reg. 8, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give consumers a fee information document before a payment account contract

summaries.en: In good time before a consumer enters into a contract for a payment account, the provider offering the account must hand the consumer a fee information document. Schedule 1 sets what the document contains and how it is presented.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Send each consumer an annual statement of fees free of charge
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), reg. 10, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Send each consumer an annual statement of fees free of charge

summaries.en: Every consumer who holds a payment account must receive from the provider, free of charge, a statement of fees once a year. The way it is sent is agreed with the consumer, and it is given on paper if the consumer asks. Schedule 2 sets its content.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Offer consumers a switching service between payment accounts
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), reg. 14, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Offer consumers a switching service between payment accounts

summaries.en: Every payment service provider must let consumers switch between payment accounts in the same currency held with providers located in the United Kingdom. The service must meet the requirements of Schedule 3 unless it is provided under an alternative arrangement that regulation 15 allows.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not discriminate between legally resident consumers who apply for or use a payment account
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), reg. 18, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Do not discriminate between legally resident consumers who apply for or use a payment account

summaries.en: When a consumer who lives lawfully in the United Kingdom applies for or uses a payment account, a credit institution may not treat that consumer differently because of nationality, place of residence or any of the personal characteristics the regulation lists, such as sex, race, religion, disability, age or sexual orientation. The conditions for holding a basic account must not be discriminatory either.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Offer a payment account with basic features to every eligible consumer
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), regs. 22 and 23, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Offer a payment account with basic features to every eligible consumer

summaries.en: A credit institution the Treasury has designated must offer a basic account to every eligible consumer who applies for one. A consumer is eligible if legally resident in the United Kingdom, which includes people with no fixed address and asylum seekers, and either holds no payment account with those features at a United Kingdom credit institution or is ineligible for the institution's other payment accounts. The institution verifies that the consumer has no such account unless it relies on the consumer's declaration.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Charge no fee for the standard sterling services of a basic account
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), reg. 20, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Charge no fee for the standard sterling services of a basic account

summaries.en: A credit institution must not charge a fee for opening, operating or closing a basic account, paying in, withdrawing cash, direct debits, card payments or credit transfers when the service is provided in sterling. It must not charge a fee when a payment fails for lack of funds, and no fee or interest when the account is overrun. For a service in another currency it may charge a reasonable fee.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Open or refuse a basic account within 10 business days and explain a refusal
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), regs. 24 and 25, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Open or refuse a basic account within 10 business days and explain a refusal

summaries.en: A designated credit institution must decide promptly whether to open a basic account, and at the latest within 10 business days of receiving the completed application. It must refuse where opening the account would be unlawful, for instance under the Fraud Act 2006, the money laundering regulations or section 40 of the Immigration Act 2014. On refusal it tells the consumer the reason in writing, free of charge and without delay where it lawfully may, and explains how to complain to it and to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Close a basic account only on the listed grounds and with the required notice
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Payment Accounts Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/2038), reg. 26, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Close a basic account only on the listed grounds and with the required notice

summaries.en: A designated credit institution may close a basic account only on a ground the regulation lists, such as knowing use for illegal purposes, no transaction for more than 24 consecutive months, incorrect information at application, loss of legal residence or a later account elsewhere with the same services. For inactivity, loss of residence or another account it gives the grounds in writing and free of charge at least two months before closure, or at least 90 days for a contract entered into on or after 28 April 2026. The notice tells the consumer how to complain to the institution and to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Deal in investments as principal only within the order's exceptions
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Excluded Activities and Prohibitions) Order 2014 (S.I. 2014/2080), arts. 4, 6 and 9, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Deal in investments as principal only within the order's exceptions

summaries.en: For a ring-fenced body, dealing in investments as principal is an excluded activity unless it falls within articles 6 to 12 of the order. The exceptions cover transactions whose sole or main purpose is to limit the body's or its group's exposure to risks such as changes in interest rates, exchange rates or prices, default risk and liquidity risk, the buying and selling of liquid assets to manage liquidity, and derivatives sold to account holders that meet the requirements of articles 10 or 11 and all the conditions in article 12.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not trade commodities as principal except for own use or as collateral
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Excluded Activities and Prohibitions) Order 2014 (S.I. 2014/2080), art. 5, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Do not trade commodities as principal except for own use or as collateral

summaries.en: Buying or selling commodities as principal is an excluded activity for a ring-fenced body. It may still deal in commodities it or a subsidiary needs for its own use or consumption, to take or realise a security interest over them, or under a title transfer collateral arrangement, and where another exception of the order applies.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Use inter-bank payment systems as a direct participant unless a listed condition is met
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Excluded Activities and Prohibitions) Order 2014 (S.I. 2014/2080), art. 13, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Use inter-bank payment systems as a direct participant unless a listed condition is met

summaries.en: A ring-fenced body must not enter into a transaction that lets it use the services of an inter-bank payment system unless it is a direct participant in that system. Otherwise one of the article's conditions has to be met: it reaches the system through a ring-fenced body of its own group that is a direct participant, it is not eligible to participate directly, it could still make its payments by another route if the intermediary failed, or the PRA has given permission.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Incur no exposure to a financial institution unless an exemption applies
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Excluded Activities and Prohibitions) Order 2014 (S.I. 2014/2080), art. 14, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Incur no exposure to a financial institution unless an exemption applies

summaries.en: A ring-fenced body may take on an exposure to a financial institution only where an exemption in article 14 or in articles 15 to 19C covers it. The exemptions include transactions whose main purpose is to hedge the body's or its group's risks and the holding of liquid assets to meet liquidity requirements, and the later articles add trade finance, securitisation and covered bonds, conduit lending, repo transactions, ancillary exposures, infrastructure financing and small exposures.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the recovery plan the content Schedule A1 requires and have the management body approve it
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Bank Recovery and Resolution (No. 2) Order 2014 (S.I. 2014/3348), Sch. A1 paras. 2, 4, 10 and 11, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give the recovery plan the content Schedule A1 requires and have the management body approve it

summaries.en: A recovery plan or group recovery plan must contain what Schedule A1 lists, among them a summary of the capacity to restore the firm's financial position, capital and liquidity actions, access to contingency funding, the critical functions, the arrangements to keep access to market infrastructure and operational processes, and a communication plan. It must not assume any access to extraordinary public financial support. It must show that the management body assessed and approved it before it went to the regulator, and must include a framework of indicators marking the points at which recovery actions may be taken.

titles.en: Monitor the recovery indicators and notify the regulator at once of a decision to depart from them

summaries.en: The plan must describe the arrangements the firm has made to monitor its recovery indicators regularly. The management body may act under the plan although an indicator has not been met, or decide not to act although one has, and the firm must notify the appropriate regulator of either decision without delay.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have an intra-group financial support agreement approved by the members and report on it every year
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Bank Recovery and Resolution (No. 2) Order 2014 (S.I. 2014/3348), arts. 98 and 100, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Have an intra-group financial support agreement approved by the members and report on it every year

summaries.en: An authorised group financial support agreement binds a United Kingdom group entity only once its members have approved it by ordinary resolution, after the directors have made available a memorandum setting out the resolution and the terms of the agreement. The directors must then prepare an annual report on how the agreement has performed and how decisions under it were implemented, and send it to every member by each anniversary of the agreement.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Offer securities to the public in the United Kingdom only where Schedule 1 allows it
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Public Offers and Admissions to Trading Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/105), reg. 12, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Offer securities to the public in the United Kingdom only where Schedule 1 allows it

summaries.en: An offer of relevant securities to the public in the United Kingdom is unlawful unless it is of a kind listed in Part 1 of Schedule 1, or consists entirely of a combination of those kinds. Part 2 of the Schedule adds supplementary provision.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give every investor in an offer the material information disclosed to selected investors
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Public Offers and Admissions to Trading Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/105), reg. 13, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give every investor in an offer the material information disclosed to selected investors

summaries.en: For an offer of relevant securities to the public of £1,000,000 or more over 12 months under the Schedule 1 exemptions the regulation names, any material information an issuer or offeror discloses to selected investors, orally or in writing, must also reach the other investors. Where the offer needs a prospectus or similar document, the information goes into that document or a supplement to it; otherwise it is shared with all the other investors the offer is aimed at.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Put in a prospectus all the information an investor needs for an informed assessment
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Public Offers and Admissions to Trading Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/105), reg. 23, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Put in a prospectus all the information an investor needs for an informed assessment

summaries.en: A prospectus, like an MTF admission prospectus, has to include the information material to an investor for an informed view of the financial position, results, assets, liabilities and prospects of the issuer and any guarantor, of the rights attached to the securities, and of the reasons for the issue and its effect on the issuer. For debt securities prospects are read as creditworthiness, and the information may vary with the issuer, the securities and the circumstances.

obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Securitisation Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/102), reg. 8A(1), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: As originator or sponsor, do not use a special purpose entity in a high-risk jurisdiction

summaries.en: The originator and the sponsor of a securitisation must make sure that it is not carried out through a securitisation special purpose entity established outside the United Kingdom in a country the Financial Action Task Force currently lists as a high-risk jurisdiction subject to a call for enhanced due diligence or for countermeasures.

obligations.title: Add the duty: As an institutional investor, do not invest in a securitisation through a high-risk jurisdiction
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Securitisation Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/102), reg. 8A(2), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: As an institutional investor, do not invest in a securitisation through a high-risk jurisdiction

summaries.en: Institutional investors may not put money into a securitisation that uses a securitisation special purpose entity established outside the United Kingdom in a country on the Financial Action Task Force's list of high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for enhanced due diligence or for countermeasures.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Use the STS label only for a securitisation that qualifies for it
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Securitisation Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/102), reg. 12, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Use the STS label only for a securitisation that qualifies for it

summaries.en: An originator, sponsor or securitisation special purpose entity may call its securitisation simple, transparent and standardised, use the term STS or any designation referring to those terms, only if it is an STS securitisation, an overseas STS securitisation of a country designated by Treasury regulations, or a qualifying EU securitisation notified to ESMA and listed by it before 11 p.m. on 30 June 2026.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Take reasonable care that nobody under a temporary management ban takes management decisions
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Securitisation Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/102), reg. 38, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Take reasonable care that nobody under a temporary management ban takes management decisions

summaries.en: An originator, sponsor or securitisation special purpose entity must take reasonable care that no individual holds an office or position with responsibility for management decisions in breach of a temporary prohibition the FCA or the PRA has imposed under regulation 37.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the borrower the pre-contract credit information on the standard form in good time
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Consumer Credit (Disclosure of Information) Regulations 2010 (S.I. 2010/1013), regs. 3 and 8, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give the borrower the pre-contract credit information on the standard form in good time

summaries.en: In good time before a regulated consumer credit agreement is made, the creditor must disclose the pre-contract credit information listed in regulation 3(4), such as the type and total amount of credit, the duration, the rate of interest, the APR and the total amount payable. It uses the form in Schedule 1, in writing and in a form the borrower can take away, completed as the notes to the form require, and gives any additional information in a separate document. It need not repeat what a credit intermediary has already disclosed in the same way.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Disclose the required credit information in telephone and other distance sales
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Consumer Credit (Disclosure of Information) Regulations 2010 (S.I. 2010/1013), regs. 4 and 5, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Disclose the required credit information in telephone and other distance sales

summaries.en: For an agreement made by telephone as a distance contract, the creditor may give a shorter set of information beforehand only if the borrower explicitly consents: the caller's identity, the main characteristics of the credit, the total price and the right to withdraw or cancel. After any telephone agreement, and after an agreement made at the borrower's request by another means of distance communication that does not allow disclosure beforehand, the full pre-contract credit information follows on the Schedule 1 form immediately.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the pre-contract information required for an authorised non-business overdraft
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Consumer Credit (Disclosure of Information) Regulations 2010 (S.I. 2010/1013), reg. 10, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Give the pre-contract information required for an authorised non-business overdraft

summaries.en: The creditor must give the borrower, in good time before it agrees an authorised non-business overdraft with the borrower, the information regulation 10(3) lists, including the type of credit, the creditor's identity, the total amount and duration of credit, the interest rate and its conditions, how the agreement can be ended, whether repayment on demand may be required and the charges for late payment and default, in the manner regulation 11 sets.

obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Consumer Credit (Agreements) Regulations 2010 (S.I. 2010/1014), reg. 3, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Put the prescribed information and the statutory statements in every regulated credit agreement

summaries.en: The document embodying a regulated consumer credit agreement must contain the information in Schedule 1 for that type of agreement, presented clearly and concisely, legible and in a colour distinct from the background. It must also contain the statements of the borrower's protection and remedies in the forms of Schedule 2, unless the agreement is exempted, and details of any security the borrower gives.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have the agreement signed in the prescribed manner with the prescribed terms
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Consumer Credit (Agreements) Regulations 2010 (S.I. 2010/1014), reg. 4, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Have the agreement signed in the prescribed manner with the prescribed terms

summaries.en: The terms in paragraphs 5, 6, 7, 11 and 14 of Schedule 1 are the prescribed terms that must appear in the document if the agreement is not to be improperly executed. The document must have a space for the borrower's signature, and the borrower and the creditor sign it in the way the regulation sets, with the dates inserted.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set out the required terms of an authorised overdraft in writing
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Consumer Credit (Agreements) Regulations 2010 (S.I. 2010/1014), reg. 8, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Set out the required terms of an authorised overdraft in writing

summaries.en: For an authorised business or non-business overdraft agreement, the creditor must set out in writing, clearly and concisely, the type of credit, the parties' identities and addresses, the duration, the credit limit and drawdown conditions, the interest rate and its conditions, the total charge for credit, any right to demand full repayment at any time and the charges payable.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Send small business credit information to a designated credit reference agency that asks for it
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Small and Medium Sized Business (Credit Information) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1945), reg. 3, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Send small business credit information to a designated credit reference agency that asks for it

summaries.en: A designated bank must provide the credit information it holds on each small or medium sized business customer that has agreed to it, when a designated credit reference agency makes a valid written request. It provides the information within 30 days of the request and updates it every month afterwards unless the agency says it no longer needs updates, adding customers who have newly agreed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Include the customer's agreement to credit information sharing in the standard terms
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Small and Medium Sized Business (Credit Information) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1945), reg. 5, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Include the customer's agreement to credit information sharing in the standard terms

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep records showing compliance for at least five years
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Small and Medium Sized Business (Credit Information) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1945), reg. 24, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

obligations.title: Add the duty: Refer a rejected small business finance application to every designated finance platform
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Small and Medium Sized Business (Finance Platforms) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1946), regs. 3 and 5, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Refer a rejected small business finance application to every designated finance platform

summaries.en: When a small or medium sized business's application for finance to a designated bank fails and the business agrees, the bank must send all the specified information it holds on the application to all designated finance platforms by the end of the working day after the business confirms its agreement. The duty does not apply to facilities under £1,000 or for less than 30 days, to applications made through a broker, or where the business faces payment proceedings or a formal demand.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Ask a rejected small business whether it agrees to a referral and otherwise send it the platforms information
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Small and Medium Sized Business (Finance Platforms) Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/1946), reg. 4, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Ask a rejected small business whether it agrees to a referral and otherwise send it the platforms information

summaries.en: When the bank tells the business that its application has failed, or by the end of the next working day after the business rejects the bank's offer, it must ask whether the business agrees to its information going to the platforms and ask for any specified information it does not hold. If the business does not agree, the bank sends it the generic platforms information within five working days of asking.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Apply the CRS and FATCA due diligence procedures to identify reportable accounts
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/878), reg. 3(1) and (2), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Apply the CRS and FATCA due diligence procedures to identify reportable accounts

summaries.en: A reporting financial institution must put in place, and keep, arrangements designed to identify, for each financial account, where the account holder and any controlling person are resident for tax purposes and whether the account is reportable. It does so by applying the due diligence procedures of the Common Reporting Standard or the FATCA agreement, as the case requires.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep records of the due diligence steps and the information collected for five years
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/878), reg. 3(2A) and (2B), revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep records of the due diligence steps and the information collected for five years

summaries.en: The institution must record the steps it took to meet its due diligence duty and the information it collected in doing so. It keeps the records for five years from the end of the year in which a reportable account was last included in a return, or, for an account treated as not reportable, from the end of the last year in which it relied on the procedures to treat it that way.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File the annual CRS and FATCA return with HMRC by 31 May
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/878), reg. 6, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: File the annual CRS and FATCA return with HMRC by 31 May

summaries.en: For every calendar year the institution must make a return to HMRC with the information the relevant agreement requires on each reportable account it maintained during the year and each pre-existing account it identified as reportable. The return is submitted electronically by 31 May of the following year.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell individual account holders by 31 January that their information will be reported
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/878), reg. 10, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Tell individual account holders by 31 January that their information will be reported

summaries.en: The institution must tell each individual reportable person or specified US person that information about them will be reported to HMRC and may be passed to the government of another territory under the relevant agreement. It does so by 31 January of the year after the first year in which the individual's account is reportable.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with HMRC as a reporting or specified non-reporting financial institution
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/878), reg. 10A, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Register with HMRC as a reporting or specified non-reporting financial institution

summaries.en: Reporting financial institutions and specified non-reporting financial institutions alike must give HMRC notice of registration in the form it directs, by the later of 31 December 2025 and 31 January of the year after the calendar year in which it first comes within the relevant definition.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep responsibility for due diligence and reporting when a service provider does the work
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Compliance Regulations 2015 (S.I. 2015/878), reg. 12, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Keep responsibility for due diligence and reporting when a service provider does the work

summaries.en: A reporting financial institution may have a service provider carry out its due diligence and reporting obligations, but they remain the institution's own obligations.

obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Enforcement (Disclosable Arrangements) Regulations 2023 (S.I. 2023/38), regs. 3, 4 and 10, text as made, the only version legislation.gov.uk holds for it

titles.en: Report a CRS avoidance arrangement or opaque offshore structure to HMRC within 30 days

summaries.en: An intermediary that makes such an arrangement or structure available for implementation, or provides relevant services in respect of it, and that acts through a United Kingdom branch or office or is resident, managed or incorporated in the United Kingdom, must make a return to HMRC with the information the model rules require, as far as it knows or holds it. The return is made electronically within 30 days beginning with the day after the arrangement was made available or the services were supplied.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell the other intermediaries and taxpayers within 30 days that a return was made
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Enforcement (Disclosable Arrangements) Regulations 2023 (S.I. 2023/38), reg. 9, text as made, the only version legislation.gov.uk holds for it

titles.en: Tell the other intermediaries and taxpayers within 30 days that a return was made

summaries.en: An intermediary or reportable taxpayer that has made a return must give written notice of that fact, within 30 days of the return, to everyone it is aware of, or ought reasonably to be aware of, as another intermediary or reportable taxpayer for that arrangement or structure.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give HMRC the information and documents a notice requires to check compliance
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The International Tax Enforcement (Disclosable Arrangements) Regulations 2023 (S.I. 2023/38), reg. 11, text as made, the only version legislation.gov.uk holds for it

titles.en: Give HMRC the information and documents a notice requires to check compliance

summaries.en: An officer of HMRC who reasonably suspects that a person is an intermediary or reportable taxpayer may require information or documents by written notice to check compliance, and the person must provide them within the period the notice sets, which is at least 30 days, by the means and in the form reasonably required.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Store or read information on a user's device only with consent or under an exception
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2426), reg. 6 and Sch. A1 paras. 2, 4 and 5, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Store or read information on a user's device only with consent or under an exception

summaries.en: No one may place information on a subscriber's or user's device, or read information already held on it, which includes collecting what the device sends out automatically, unless an exception in Schedule A1 applies. The main exception is that the user has clear and comprehensive information about the purpose and gives consent, which may be signified through browser settings; others cover storage strictly necessary for the service the user asked for and, with information and a free means to object, statistics used to improve the service or website.

obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2426), reg. 19, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Make automated marketing calls only to subscribers who have consented

summaries.en: A recorded marketing message may be sent through an automated calling or communication system only to a line whose subscriber has told the caller that it consents for the time being, and only if the caller shows its calling line identity or a number on which it can be contacted.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Show the caller's number and respect objections and the preference register on marketing calls
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2426), reg. 21, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Show the caller's number and respect objections and the preference register on marketing calls

summaries.en: Anyone making marketing calls must not hide the calling line identity and must present a number on which it can be contacted. It must not make unsolicited marketing calls to a subscriber who has asked not to receive them or to a number listed on the register kept under regulation 26 for at least 28 days, unless that subscriber has told the caller it does not object to its calls.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Send marketing emails and texts to individuals only with consent or under the existing customer exception
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2426), reg. 22, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Send marketing emails and texts to individuals only with consent or under the existing customer exception

summaries.en: Unsolicited marketing by electronic mail, which includes text messages, may be sent to an individual subscriber only if the recipient has told the sender that it consents for the time being. The exception allows marketing of the sender's own similar products and services to a person whose details it obtained in a sale or negotiations for a sale, provided the person was given a simple, free way to refuse when the details were collected and in every later message.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Never disguise the sender of marketing email and always give a valid address to opt out
obligations.sourceLabel: legislation.gov.uk, The Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (S.I. 2003/2426), reg. 23, revised text as it stands on 2026-11-14

titles.en: Never disguise the sender of marketing email and always give a valid address to opt out
